keyFindings.description: Rule 6b recognises only always() where GitHub suppresses the implicit success() for any of its four status functions, so the required lint job refuses the !cancelled() shape that would close the accepted cancelled-run exposure, and the 6b message and AGENTS.md:127 assert GitHub's semantics for that refusal. The plan decided always()-only explicitly (plan.md: 'If the architect wants !cancelled(), rule 6 accepts it beside always()'), so this is the architect's rule decision, not a defect in this PR; the wording goes in the fast-follow.

Two mutation holes in the harness: deleting the '"if" in jobs[ancestor]' filter (6b's skippable predicate) or scoping the rule-6 loop to RELEASE leaves 221/221 green. The lint job's run on the real workflows catches the first (the three *_build conditions would be named); nothing catches the second. A green case for a plain if: on an if:-less ancestor chain and one rule-6 case on $INFRA close both.

A needs: entry that is not a string (a nested list) aborts the checker with a TypeError traceback, suppressing the file's other ::error:: lines. Fail-closed, and GitHub refuses such a workflow at parse; filter needs_of to strings.
6a's missing list dedupes on the original spelling while tested lowercases, so a mixed-case double read is named twice in the message; the verdict is unaffected.

The comment reads as if the old condition were broken; build is publish's only ancestor, so the old implicit success() skipped it only when wanted. The rewrite is rule-6 conformance (and the cancelled-run delta), not a fix.

legion_publish now publishes in a run where envoy_plugin_publish failed (pi_envoy_publish:814 makes that a skipped pi_envoy_publish, legion_build:241 accepts skipped); the header comment discusses skipped upstreams only. Pre-split design restored, and pi_legion_publish:1007 already behaves so; one sentence in the header would name it.
